subject: Map parameter names in stan code to original parameter names

messages.author: 57338e36f04c0bcf
messages.subject: Map parameter names in stan code to original parameter names
parts:
Hi Paul,


I am new to multilevel modeling and I'm trying to use the stan code and data generated by brms as input for CmdStan. (The dataset is quite large and directly running the model using brms gave a memory error). I had some trouble trying to map the parameter names in the generated stan code to the original parameter names. 


Here is what I did and I tested my code on a smaller dataset. I first generated the stan code and data:


d = read.csv('nod2.txt', header=TRUE, sep="\t" )

bf_rarevariant <- bf(BETA|se(SE) ~  1 + (0 + POPULATION|VARID) + (0 + DISEASE|VARID), family='gaussian')

scode = make_stancode(bf_rarevariant, data=d, save_model=‘model.stan’)

sdat = make_standata(bf_rarevariant, data=d)

for (i in seq(length(sdat))) {

  assign(names(sdat)[i], sdat[[i]])

}

stan_rdump(names(sdat), file='model.data.R')



And then compile the model and ran the executable and summarize the samples using CmdStan:



./model variational algorithm=meanfield iter=10000 \

          random seed=1234              \

          data file=model.data.R \

          output file=samples.csv

$cmdStan/bin/stansummary --csv_file=summary.csv samples.csv



And then I tried to map the variables in the stan summary file to original parameter name (used code from rename_pars.R):



vb.summary <- read.csv('summary.csv', header=T, stringsAsFactors=F)

pars <- as.character(vb.summary$name)

bterms <- parse_bf(bf_rarevariant)

data <- update_data(d, bterms)

meef <- tidy_meef(bterms, data=data)

ranef <- tidy_ranef(bterms, data=data)


change <- c(

  change_effects(bterms, data = data, pars = pars, scode = scode),

  change_re(ranef, pars = pars),

  change_Xme(meef, pars = pars),

  change_autocor(bterms, data = data, pars = pars)

)


names.stan <- c()

names.model <- c()

for (i in seq(length(change))) {

  names.stan <- c(names.stan, pars[change[[i]]$pos])

  names.model <- c(names.model, change[[i]]$fnames)

}


map <- hashmap(names.stan, names.model)



However, it didn’t recover all the names (length of names.stan is 529 and length of pars is 1085). In addition, when I ran the model directly in brms on the same dataset and it gave a warning message:



fit <- brm(BETA|se(SE) ~  1 + (0 + POPULATION|VARID) + (0 + DISEASE|VARID), data=d,

           algorithm='meanfield', iter=1000)


Warning message:

  In names(x$fit@sim$samples[[i]])[change$pos] <- change$fnames :

  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length


And running length(fit$fit@sim$fnames_oi) also only returns 529. I was wondering why the number of parameters doesn't match up and is there an easier way to get the names mapped?
